features.note: REAR shot: the DIN spring-clip reads clearly at the intended rear dimness (rear/front 0.48) — the hook, the stepped leaf spring (which catches a highlight), and the screwdriver tab all legible. The rig keeps the rear critical readable while still darker than the front, so depth is preserved without hiding the feature.

10 recessed jacks read clearly in 5x2; the mix is built and guarded. RESIDUAL: after three levers (material collar -> geometry sleeve -> front fill 0.30->0.45, front/side contrast measured 1.63->1.73 so the recess read did NOT flatten), the silver SFP sleeve on column 5 still does not POP strongly against the lit grey cavities at this exposure. This does not fail the critical (the jacks and the built mix are present; the RJ45/SFP distinction is genuinely subtle at real-world scale too). Builder named the honest limit: the analytic model proves a lamp AIMS into the throat but cannot prove how much light survives occlusion — capture is the arbiter, and it reads soft. Next lever is the sleeve's envMapIntensity (bare metal responds to environment more than to any directional). Treated as OPTIONAL final polish, not a blocker.
Front LED column well-lit; labels read. No regression.

THE POINT OF THIS PASS. The rig arrived as a LITERAL COPY of the PDU rig, whose key was deliberately LOWERED because that subject was a 1.78 m vertical bar with all identity on one plane and up-facing light was wasted. This subject is the opposite: a compact box with a critical ON THE TOP FACE (the screw terminal blocks) and a 42/24 hero chosen to show front and top together. Dragging that rig unexamined would have darkened a critical to solve a problem this subject does not have. Builder re-aimed: TOP +y irradiance 1.293 -> 1.500 (+16%), front 1.696 -> 1.742. The three terminal blocks with screw heads now read bright and clear against the lit top face. Same house rig, correct opposite answer.
Livery reads well under the front key; no wash-out, no dead shadow. No regression.

defects: SFP sleeve still reads soft at capture after three levers; the analytic rig can aim light into the throat but cannot model occlusion survival. Non-blocking (port-block-10 passes). Optional final lever: sleeve envMapIntensity. Recommend ONE attempt during optimization/P6-prep and then stop chasing — the RJ45/SFP distinction is subtle in reality.
Overall exposure is on the moody/dark side — appropriate for the aisle context but a touch dark for a standalone hero; acceptable.
corrections: Optional (before P6): raise the SFP sleeve envMapIntensity once to see if the silver mouth pops; if it does not clearly help, leave it — do not add more lamps.
Interaction-ui pass: capture --page (the DOM UI is the deliverable).

mechanical.notes: Console clean (0/0) across default, port-detail, rear, leds. Framing default fullyVisible/wellFramed/no-HUD. Budget unchanged (36/150 draws, 1828/200000 tris — lighting adds no geometry). Four rig criteria are now ASSERTED in the check so a later pass cannot silently detune the rig: front/top in [1.05, 1.25], rear/front >= 0.40, flank separation >= 1.5 (the louvres need one lit flank and one shadowed to throw their line), front/side >= 1.3. Builder self-caught a real error: his header-block edit deleted the THREE import in lighting.mjs and it reached the real file, not just the sandbox copy — caught because the lighting check IMPORTS and EXERCISES the module and it threw (a syntax --check would have passed that file). Argues for checks that exercise, not just lint.

notes: Inline orchestrator judgment. The pass's core job — the rig — is right: the builder recognized the inherited PDU rig would have under-lit this subject's TOP-face critical and re-aimed it analytically (+16% top), so all criticals are now lit (front, top, and a readable rear at appropriate dimness) with no blown highlights or dead shadows, and the four balance ratios are asserted against future drift. One residual soft spot (SFP pop) is non-blocking with a named optional lever. Cleared to the interaction-ui pass.
